title: Prompt Economy Accordion — draft notes
body:
High-level idea (one line):
An accordion-style prompt UI + runtime policy that expands response fidelity (and cost) progressively only when the user or runtime signals value — making per-interaction token spend more predictable and reclaimable.

Context / problem statement:
- Engineers building assistants want predictable per-interaction costs while preserving the ability to escalate to richer outputs when needed.
- Current approaches: blunt tiering (cheap/standard/premium) or manual prompts that cost unpredictable tokens when long contexts are sent.
- We can provide a UX + runtime contract that lets product teams present an expandable response plan: start low-cost, then optionally expand with additional compute/quality steps.

Core components (sketch):
1) Accordion UI model (frontend):
   - Primary (collapsed) response: single-shot terse answer or structured summary (e.g., 1–2 sentences, small token budget).
   - Secondary (expand) layers: progressively richer outputs (longer narrative, code generation, deeper reasoning) fetched on demand.
   - Each layer shows incremental cost estimate (tokens/cost) and latency range.

2) Runtime contract / API options:
   - request.fidelity = [baseline|expandable] plus an optional expansion_token that can be spent later.
   - expansion_token = conservative pre-authorized micro-bill allowing N additional tokens at a capped price, or an on-demand charge flow that asks user for confirmation.
   - server-side supports staged generation: prefix-only baseline, then continuation checkpoints for expanded generation using KV cache to avoid redoing earlier compute.

3) Serving optimizations (what runtime must do):
   - checkpointable generation (warm KV caches and resume), fast-stitching of baseline->expanded outputs with minimal recompute.
   - budgeted continuations: allocate a small, higher-priority slot for expansions to keep latency reasonable.
   - metrics to measure expected spend vs actual spend, and fidelity utility (human-rated).

Why it fits Redwood:
- Matches our strength: model variants, routing policies, and caching reduce cost for stepped responses.
- Gives customers clear levers for cost control (pre-commit tokens, expansion caps, token budgets per user).
- UI + API consistency across hosted/dedicated/private (frontends can implement accordion while runtime provides same resume/continuation primitives).

User stories (rough):
- As an end user, I want a short answer quickly and the option to ask for a longer explanation so I don't incur higher costs unless I want it.
- As a product manager, I want to show an estimated cost and latency for each expansion layer so we can balance conversion vs cost.
- As an engineer, I want an API that optionally returns a resumable generation_id so I can request an expanded result without resending huge contexts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Frontend: collapsible response with two layers (baseline + one expand), UI shows incremental cost estimate.
- API: support "resume_id" returned with baseline responses and an endpoint to request expansion by resume_id.
- Runtime: resume endpoint uses cached KV to continue generation without re-encoding the whole prompt; observed recompute < 25% of tokens.
- Metrics: dashboards for expansion rate, incremental spend per expansion, latency percentiles for expansions.

Experimentation plan / metrics to watch:
- Expansion rate (percent of baseline responses that users expand). Target initial hypothesis: 10–20% for help-style apps, 2–5% for search-style.
- Incremental spend per expanded session and ROI (measured by feature engagement / conversion).
- Latency of expansion (p95) — target < 800ms for user-initiated expand on Dedicated pools.

Design notes / wireframe thoughts:
- Each collapsed response shows a subtle "Expand for more" affordance with an estimated +$0.00X. Clicking triggers a toast with a short confirmation if expansion_token not pre-authorized.
- Optionally allow auto-expand for certain triggers (user has premium flag or confidence low/high).

Edge cases & open Qs:
- What if expansion depends on a changed context (user added new instruction)? Need to either invalidate resume_id or re-encode diff. Runtime should accept a short diff to re-attach to cached KV (complex).
- Authorization UX: will product teams accept micro-billing UX? Some prefer trusted reserved budgets. We need both flows.
- How do we handle hallucination corrections across expansions? If baseline is terse, expansion must be consistent; need markers to chain generations or deterministic seeds.
- Billing model: charge on expansion only (preferred) or reserve small authorization upfront (reduces friction?). Consider per-customer configurable policy.

Implementation dependencies / risks:
- Requires checkpointable/resumable generation primitives (runtime & model support). Risk: some open models or quantized backends may not support fast resume without full recompute.
- Metrics plumbing: need to tag baseline vs expansion token consumption per request to attribute spend correctly.
- UX: designers required to craft non-scary cost messaging.

Rollout strategy (phases):
- Phase 0 (lab): internal dogfood with docs team; baseline+one expansion, logs-only billing (no real charge).
- Phase 1 (beta): opt-in for select customers; allow pre-authorized expansion_token and measure expansion rates.
- Phase 2 (GA): expose as togglable feature in Console with per-route config, expand caps, and analytics.

Open tasks / TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- Spike: prototype resume_id + minimal KV replay with Anton (serving-runtime).
- UX: quick mockups for collapsible response and micro-billing flows (owner: Maya).
- Legal: get buy-in on micro-charge phrasing / TOS implications (owner: Kai).
- PM: draft PRD skeleton for beta (owner: me) and link to INF-2741.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep the first public surface conservative: show cost-estimate in cents, not fractions, to feel tangible.
- Consider a "confidence-aware auto-expand" where high-uncertainty queries auto-enable the next layer. Track false-positive expansions.
- Evaluate fallback: if resume fails, gracefully fall back to full re-gen with user-visible warning and soft cap.

Links & references (scraps):
- Slack thread: #product-fidelity (pinned message id 3782)
- Past experiments: ticket INF-1898 (half-token progressive answers)

Random brainstorming bullets (untamed):
- "Accordion coupons": occasional free expansions to train behavior.
- "Cheap previews": small extracted facts as baseline then full narrative on expand (good for news summarizers).
- Per-user daily expansion budget to prevent runaway costs for free tiers.

If anyone is reading this and wants to help with the spike: ping me (Ethan) or add to INF-2741.

-- end of notes --
